bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Anesthesiologist Salary in Australia

If you're researching the **anesthesiologist salary** in Australia, you're looking at one of the highest-paid medical specialties. According to the latest data from Jobs and Skills Australia (powered by the Australian Bureau of Statistics), the median weekly earnings for anaesthetists are $8,293, with a median hourly rate of $218. Most anaesthetists work full-time (90% of the profession) and average 46 hours per week. This guide explains how to convert that hourly rate to annual pay, what it means for your fortnightly take-home, and how it compares to the National Minimum Wage and award rates.

### How to Convert Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

The standard formula for annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For an anesthesiologist earning the median $218 per hour and working 46 hours per week:

$218 × 46 × 52 = $521,456 per year

However, many people prefer to use the standard full-time week of 38 hours for comparison. Using 38 hours:

$218 × 38 × 52 = $430,768 per year

This is the figure you'll often see in salary surveys. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page on this site lets you plug in any rate and hours to see your own estimate.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For the median anesthesiologist working 46 hours:

- Weekly: $8,293
- Fortnightly: $16,586

If you're paid a salary rather than hourly, you can divide your annual salary by 26 to get a fortnightly figure. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator can help estimate what lands in your bank after tax.

### How Anesthesiologist Pay Compares to Minimum and Award Rates

It's important to distinguish the anesthesiologist salary from the National Minimum Wage and typical award rates. The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage at $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees get a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour.

Anesthesiologists are not covered by a modern award in the usual sense—they are typically employed under enterprise agreements or individual contracts that far exceed minimum rates. The median hourly rate of $218 is over eight times the minimum wage. For comparison, the ABS Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time earnings (May 2026) is $2,083.70 per week, or about $54.83 per hour based on 38 hours. An anesthesiologist's weekly earnings of $8,293 are nearly four times that average.

### Superannuation on Top

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For an anesthesiologist earning $521,456, the super would be capped at $270,830 × 12% = $32,499.60 per year. If using the 38-hour annual figure of $430,768, the super would be $430,768 × 12% = $51,692.16, but because that exceeds the cap, it would be limited to $32,499.60. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Tax on an Anesthesiologist Salary

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds).

For an annual salary of $521,456 (46-hour week), the tax would be approximately:

- $0 on $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 = $4,020
- 30% on $90,000 = $27,000
- 37% on $55,000 = $20,350
- 45% on $331,456 = $149,155.20
- Total tax: $200,525.20
- Medicare levy (2%): $10,429.12
- Total deductions: $210,954.32
- Net annual: $310,501.68

This is a rough estimate. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page can give a more personalised calculation.

### Important Considerations

- **Actual hours vary**: Some anaesthetists work more or fewer than 46 hours. The median is a guide only.
- **Penalty rates and overtime**: The anesthesiologist salary often includes on-call and after-hours work, which may attract higher rates. This estimate assumes the same hourly rate for all hours.
- **Salary packaging**: Many doctors use salary packaging for cars, super, or other benefits, which can reduce taxable income.
- **Award vs agreement**: While most anaesthetists are above award, some junior or training positions may fall under the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020. Check your specific employment contract.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

This site's [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and toggle casual loading if applicable. For anesthesiologists, casual loading is not typical, so leave the casual loading checkbox unchecked. The tool then shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures, plus estimated tax and super.

### Summary

The **anesthesiologist salary** in Australia is among the highest of any occupation, with median weekly earnings of $8,293 and a median hourly rate of $218. Using the standard 38-hour week gives an annual figure of $430,768, but actual earnings are often higher due to longer hours. Use the [reference tables](/blog) page to see how other professions stack up.
